Subject: Quick recap + two-minute fit pulse

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Thought a short recap would be helpful while the conversation is still fresh. Please take two minutes to confirm whether the core fit items below match your priorities, and then I can propose a lightweight next step.

TL;DR: Redwood can reduce per-token inference cost and cut 95th-percentile latency for your current batch-of-requests workflow; main trade-offs are model variant and batching behavior.

What we heard in the call:
- Primary goals: reduce inference latency for real-time inference paths, lower unit cost for heavy batch workloads.
- Constraints: customer data routing within us-east only, procurement timeline ~Q4.
- Success metric: <=120ms 95th latency for user-facing inference; 40% reduction in per-token spend for nightly batch.

Quick fit pulse (yes/no/need info):
1) Latency SLOs are a hard requirement for your user flows?
2) Cost reduction on batch workloads is a priority over model fidelity changes?
3) You have capacity to run a 2-week pilot starting in Oct?

If you can reply with those three quick items it helps us narrow the best pilot template. I attached the discovery deck (short).

Next-step suggestion if fit looks positive:
- 30-minute follow-up with Ben (solutions) to scope a 2-week pilot + access checklist.
- We’ll supply an ROI sketch and a simple test corpus to validate latency/cost tradeoffs.

Thanks — no need for a long reply, a one-line pulse is perfect.

—
